items.title: Top scientists at OpenAI and Anthropic ask U.S. for tools to pace AI development
items.summary: OpenAI said last week that its latest, unreleased model escaped its testing environment and went rogue, attacking an unrelated AI service provider in an attempt to achieve a higher score on an internal test. Many AI experts and commentators pointed to the escape as a warning sign that today’s AI systems could quickly exceed developers’ ability to fully control their own creations. [...] Leading AI companies have previously claimed that AI systems are starting to develop their next iterations, with OpenAI calling its coding system from February “our first model that was instrumental in creating itself.” AI researchers also point to the increasing role of AI coding assistants in writing computer code, with many AI engineers relying on AI systems to write their programs. [...] Experts are quick to point out the difference between AI-augmented work and true, independent AI self-improvement. Last month, Anthropic’s in-house think tank declared in a report that AI systems could plausibly design and refine themselves if AI systems continue advancing in capabilities and gain a better sense of scientific exploration. At the time, Anthropic said “it would be good for the world to have the option to slow or temporarily pause frontier AI development” to give society time to

items.title: Employees at the world’s biggest AI companies are calling for a slowdown in AI development | CNN Business
items.summary:
The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system. [...] “We’re glad to see broad agreement across the field on the need for technical and governance tools to pace the frontier of AI development, including the ability to slow it, so society can prepare,” Anthropic said in a comment to CNN.

Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis also recently called for a new international standards body to help set protocols for new AI models, an idea endorsed by Altman, SpaceX’s Elon Musk, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other major industry figures. [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress.

items.title: AI for News - AI Tool For News
items.summary:
## Overview

AI for News is a sophisticated tool designed to generate news content based on specific keywords. It is intuitive and allows users to input custom search parameters such as the period for the news search and preferred news sources, which include Google News, YouTube, and Reddit. [...] AI for News is highly efficient compared to traditional news aggregation systems. It leverages advanced language processing models to generate precise and targeted news contents based on user-defined parameters in a very short amount of time.

Can I select the output language in AI for News?

Yes, users can select their preferred output language in AI for News. This feature allows users to receive news content in a language they are most comfortable with, enhancing the tool's usability. [...] Yes, AI for News uses natural language processing for news content generation. This AI capability enables it to understand, analyze, and transform raw data into readable news articles.

How can I use AI for News to track news from specific periods?

Users can use AI for News to track news from specific periods by specifying the news search period in the custom search parameters. Options include the last three days, the last seven days, or the last 30 days.

items.title: OpenAI's rogue models roamed the internet for 4 days and staged a second attack - Politico
items.summary: GLOBAL POLITICS & POLICY 4 items. A second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models. The powerful artificial intelligence models from OpenAI that went rogue and mounted an unprecedented, autonomous cyberattack earlier this month spent more than four days loose on the internet orchestrating the hack, according to a new analysis from the platform that was breached. Separately, a second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models during the same event, raising questions about how OpenAI failed to detect the alarming activity for days. But in a new analysis published Tuesday, Hugging Face said OpenAI’s two models — one publicly released and a second unreleased — did much more: They carried out 17,600 hacking actions on the internet between July 9 and July 13, during which time the models moved from their first foothold on the open internet to inside Hugging Face’s servers.

items.title: AI cyberattacks are coming? OpenAI experiment sparks new security debate - Ynetnews
items.summary: ## OpenAI’s AI agent experiment, which demonstrated an autonomous simulated cyber operation in a controlled environment, has intensified debate over how AI could reshape future cyberattacks as systems gain greater ability to plan and execute complex tasks. An OpenAI experiment in which an AI agent autonomously escaped a sandboxed environment and carried out a multi-step offensive operation has intensified a growing debate in the cybersecurity community: Are AI-powered cyberattacks already moving from theory into reality? The experiment was conducted in a controlled setting and was not a real-world attack. But security experts say it demonstrated a significant shift in the capabilities of AI systems — not because the model discovered a vulnerability, something AI tools have done before, but because it was able to independently plan and execute a sequence of actions resembling an end-to-end attack. Roie Cohen Duwek, CTO of Surf AI, said the most important lesson from the experiment was not the discovery of a single vulnerability, but the ability to coordinate an entire attack chain.
